title: A TALE of SWEET genes: Transcriptomic analysis reveals the first black rot susceptibility genes in cauliflower
content: Brassica oleracea is an important vegetable crop cultivated globally. Selection for different traits in B. oleracea has resulted in impressive morphotypic diversity, and these morphotypes account for numerous household vegetables such as broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, cauliflower, kale, and kohlrabi. However, these vegetables are the hosts of several pathogens that cause yield-limiting disease. Among them, black rot, caused by the bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris (Xcc), is one of the most devastating, resulting in up to 60% yield loss in susceptible cultivars (Greer et al 2023).
